title: Derived tensor-Hom adjunction with a bimodule and retained scalars
statement:
Let $S\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Use the ordinary module derived categories $D(S),D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor and Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $E\in D(B)$, $X\in D(B)$, and $V\in D(S)$. Regard $E$ as a $B$-$S$ bimodule by restriction along $S\to B$. Write $J_E(V)\in D(B)$ for derived $S$-linear Hom from $E$ to $V$ with $B$ acting by precomposition: it is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(E^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ for a representative $E^\bullet$ of $E$ and a K-injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $V$, and $(b h)(e)=h(be)$. This is independent of representatives. With $U:D(B)\to D(S)$ the restriction functor, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$U R\operatorname{Hom}_B(X,J_E(V))\ \cong\ R\operatorname{Hom}_S\bigl(U(X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E),V\bigr).$$
It induces the tensor-Hom adjunction on morphism sets by taking $H^0$, with evaluation as counit. In particular all these comparisons remain compatible with restriction to any ring $K\to S$. No flatness of $B$ over $S$, perfectness of $E$, or boundedness of $V$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 09LN (lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential graded clause) and 09LT (lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint); ordinary commutative rings in degree zero, with the S-linear internal-Hom enhancement. The displayed enhancement follows from their chain adjunction using a K-projective B-model of X and a K-injective S-model of V.

from.place: Proof (1)--(2), semistable-alteration input in the nearby-cycle branch: ILO Exposé X, Theorem 3.4, Step 3, invoking Temkin 2010, Theorems 1.5 and 1.1 for a semistable multipointed modification. Temkin proof component: Marked dualizing line bundle and contracted-component degrees. Auxiliary input: Local complete-intersection determinant adjunction underlying the marked dualizing construction, before the marking is inserted. More precisely: coherent relative-duality polynomial-chart input; Rigidity of already given coherent relative dualizing pairs. Affine reduction and rigidity: Unnormalized isomorphism of algebraic relative dualizing objects. Repair of its affine uniqueness input: Polynomial reduction of diagonal derived Hom. Mixed-ring tensor-Hom adjunction used to move the diagonal module past the perfect polynomial dual.
